Contact ImageTo20KB

Have a question about compressing a photo or signature, found a mistake in a guide, or need to report a problem? Use the form below or email us directly. This page also explains what to include so that we can help you quickly.

Send us a message

Tell us the page address, your browser and device, and what happened. Maximum 1500 characters. Please do not include ID numbers or private documents.

Or email us directly

This form opens your own email application with the message ready to send, so nothing is sent until you press send there. If nothing opens, copy your message and email it to us at the address on this page.

Ways to contact us

The simplest way is the form above, which prepares an email for you. You can also write directly to compressimageto@gmail.com. The site has no accounts, no chat widget and no telephone line, which keeps things simple and means there is no profile of you on this site to manage.

Which topic should I choose?

Problem with the tool is for cases where a file would not load, compression failed, the result was unexpectedly large, or a button did not work. Exam photo or signature size question is for the exam pages: if you think a size range is out of date or wrong, tell us which exam, which notification and where you saw the correct figure. Correction or feedback on a guide covers the blog and help pages. Accessibility barrier is for anything that is hard to use with a keyboard, screen reader or zoom. Copyright notice and Security report are explained further below. Something else is for any other question.

What to include in your message

A good message saves a round of questions. For a tool problem, include the address of the page, the browser and device you use, the target size you chose, the format and approximate size of the original file, and what you saw. Avoid sending the image itself unless we ask for it, and never send photographs of identity documents. For a correction, include the page address, the sentence that seems wrong and a link to the official source that shows the right information. For an accessibility report, tell us which assistive technology you use.

What we can and cannot help with

We can explain how the tool behaves, suggest settings for a stubborn image, correct mistakes on the site, and look into bugs. We cannot guarantee that a particular government, exam, employer or university portal will accept a file, because those portals set and change their own rules. We cannot recover files that were deleted from your device, we do not receive your images through the tool, and we cannot give legal advice. If a portal rejects your upload, its helpdesk is the right place to ask what it requires.

Quick answers before you write

Many questions are already answered. The FAQs cover formats, quality and privacy. The blog explains why a portal may say a file is too large after compression. The government exam photo and signature page explains size ranges for SSC, RRB and UPSC style forms, and how it works describes the method and its limits.

Privacy of your message

When you use the form, your browser opens your email application and fills in the subject and message. The message travels through your own email provider to our inbox. We receive your name, email address and the text you wrote, and we use them only to reply and to keep a record of the conversation. The contact page itself does not store what you type. Read the privacy policy for the full details, including how site analytics work.

Security and copyright reports

If you believe you found a security problem, describe how to reproduce it and give us reasonable time to respond before sharing it publicly. If you believe something on the site infringes your copyright, include the page address, a description of the work and a statement that you are the owner or authorised to act. More information is on the security and copyright policy pages.

Who replies

The site is developed and managed by Kamlesh Mohabe, Software Engineer, who reads the messages. We reply when we can, but we cannot promise a response time. Learn more on the about page.
